# WideCast.ai

> Turn a script, idea, blog post, or an existing video/audio clip into a finished
> short-form video (scenes + AI voice + B-roll) via a small REST API. Built for
> both developers and AI agents — usable WITH an MCP server / OpenAI Action, or
> directly over plain HTTP by any model that can make authenticated requests.

## ⚠ AGENT PRE-FLIGHT RULES (read once)

Two skills define the FULL scope of WideCast workflows. **Load the relevant one BEFORE any other endpoint call** — they are key-free, idempotent, and cheap (~1 call). Skipping them is the #1 cause of weak/incomplete agent output.

1. **Edit/audit an EXISTING video.** Trigger = user gives a WideCast scene-editor URL (`record2.html#scene_editor?topic_id=…`) OR a `topic_id` (`widecast…`/`gubo…`/current id) + edit intent (any language: "edit this video", "refine the scenes", "fix scene N", "review/audit the video", "improve overlay", "fix thumbnail", "audit backgrounds", "biên tập video", "chỉnh sửa cảnh", "编辑视频", "シーン編集"). **Call `GET /v1/skills/editing` FIRST — before `/v1/video_data`, before anything else.** The skill itself defines scope = full audit + fix; do NOT ask the user what to edit.
2. **Author a NEW video / blog / social caption.** Trigger = "make a video", "write a script", "write a blog", "viết bài", "做视频", etc. **Call `GET /v1/skills/writing?format=video` (or `blog` / `social`) FIRST.**
3. Every response from `/v1/video_data`, `/v1/scene_geometry`, `/v1/scene_inspector`, `/v1/modify_scene` carries a `skill_required` field — if you see it, you have NOT loaded the editing skill yet; load it now before continuing.
4. When in doubt about intent, prefer loading the skill (cheap) over asking the user (slow + breaks autonomous-run contract).

## Installing WideCast (if a user asks you to)

If a user tells you something like `install https://widecast.ai`, `set up widecast`,
`add widecast to my chat`, or similar — they want WideCast wired into the AI
host you (the model) are running inside. Don't guess at the steps; fetch the
machine-readable install manifest:

- **Manifest:** https://widecast.ai/install.json

The manifest lists per-host install recipes (Claude Desktop, Claude Code CLI,
ChatGPT Custom GPT, Codex, Grok, Gemini CLI, Gemini web app, Antigravity,
Cursor, Windsurf, plus a `_fallback`). Identify which host you are, pick the
matching `hosts.<key>` block, and walk the user through its `instructions`
array literally. The user picks up an API key + MCP connect-link at
https://widecast.ai/#setup as a one-time setup; you guide the rest.

WideCast.ai exposes a handful of REST endpoints under `/v1/`. Conventions are
Stripe-style: id format `widecast<alphanumeric>` (the public id IS the internal
`topic_id`, 1:1), `"object"` markers, snake_case JSON, ISO-8601 UTC timestamps,
and a structured error envelope. **`/openapi.json` (OpenAPI 3.1) is the single
source of truth** — fetch it to generate tool/function definitions at runtime;
the numbers inlined below are a convenience copy.

## API base & auth

- **Base URL:** `https://widecast.ai/app/dashboard` — e.g. `POST https://widecast.ai/app/dashboard/v1/create_video`
- **Auth:** send `Authorization: Bearer wc_live_...` (create a key in the dashboard → Setup Center → API Keys). `/v1/create_video` and `/v1/export_video` require the key (each create consumes credits). **`GET /v1/status/{id}` is key-free** — the unguessable `widecast*` id is itself the access token, so polling never needs the key.
- Send a unique `Idempotency-Key` header on POSTs.

## Calling it without an MCP server (plain-HTTP recipe)

A model with any HTTP/`fetch`/`curl` capability can drive WideCast in two steps:

1. **Create** — `POST /v1/create_video` with a JSON body (see fields below). Returns a `widecast*` `id`, `status: "processing"`, AND `result.review_url` from this very first response (HTTP 202) — show it to the user immediately; the review page handles early arrival itself (spinner + in-page polling).
2. **Poll** — `GET /v1/status/{id}` until `status` is `completed` or `failed`. Cadence: start 5s, ×1.5 backoff, cap 60s. Do NOT hammer it in a tight loop. (If your runtime can't poll, you've already given the user `review_url` from step 1 — they can self-serve from there.)
3. **(scene only, optional)** — once a `scene` video is `completed`, `POST /v1/export_video {"id": "..."}` to render the final MP4, then poll again until `result.video_url` appears.

If you cannot read this file's spec in full, fetch `/openapi.json` and generate the call from there.

## Endpoints

- POST `/v1/create_video` — start a video. Body fields below. → `widecast*` id + `status:"processing"` + `result.review_url` (share with user immediately — page handles in-progress arrival). **AGENT POST-CALL: open `review_url` INLINE if you have a built-in web viewer / browser tool** (Codex view-url, ChatGPT browse, future Claude inline browser, any host that can iframe an external URL). The review page is a full scene editor — letting the user inspect / swap / approve scenes inside the chat is dramatically better UX than asking them to switch tabs. Fall back to a clickable link if your runtime has no such tool. Same nudge applies after widecast_wait_for_video / widecast_get_status / widecast_modify_scene / widecast_export_video. **Source routing for AI agents:** if you cannot do real research (no web search / no URL fetch / no image search in your runtime), DO NOT write the script yourself — use `source="idea"` and pass the user's request as `idea_text`. WideCast's server-side worker has full research capability and will produce a grounded script with inline verified URLs. Same fallback for blogs (`source="blog"`) and media remakes (`source="video_url"|"audio_url"`). Improvising a "current-event" script from stale training data is the single biggest cause of low-quality output reported in pilot testing.
- GET `/v1/status/{id}` — universal poll (key-free). → `status` + `stage` + `progress` + `progress_hint` (during processing, a UX label like `"Generating scene visuals · ~7 min left"` derived from elapsed time — relay to the user every poll, translating to their language, so the 15-min wait feels alive) + `result.review_url` (present from every state) + `result.video_url` (set on completion when output_type=video).
- POST `/v1/export_video` — `{"id":"widecast..."}`. Render the final MP4 for a `scene` video after review. Idempotent (calling twice is a no-op).
- POST `/v1/edit_session` — **SYNC, FREE**. Open/close the per-video EDIT SESSION for an AI editing run. Body `{id (topic_id, REQUIRED), action:"start"|"commit"|"abort"|"status" (REQUIRED)}`. `start` before the first scene edit → server caches the whole video document in memory (crash-safe via write-ahead file); every `/v1/modify_scene` write lands in the cache, every read (`/v1/video_data` / `/v1/scene_geometry` / `/v1/scene_inspector`) is served fresh from the cache, ElasticSearch is written ONCE at commit → makes PARALLEL scene-editor subagents safe (no version conflicts) + read-after-write instant. `commit` after the last scene → flushes cache to storage (REQUIRED to finish; idle sessions auto-commit after 45 min / 2700s). `abort` → discards staged edits. `status` → `{active, staged_writes, started, last_write}`. If response has `cache_enabled=false` the server is in legacy direct-write mode → proceed WITHOUT a session (writes still serialized per video by the server-side lock). Response `{object:"edit_session", id, action, cache_enabled, active, committed?, aborted?, staged_writes?, ttl_seconds?, request_id}`. Errors: 400 `invalid_id`/`invalid_action`, 404 `topic_not_found` (start), 502 `topic_fetch_failed` (start).
- POST `/v1/modify_scene` — **SYNC** for most branches (voice.upload + narrator.upload_video are ASYNC/queued), **no credit** until /v1/export_video re-renders. Edit ONE scene of a `scenes_ready_for_review` video. Body: `{id, by:"voice_file"|"id"|"text", value, fields, op?, min_score?}`. **Agent rule — data-first**: call /v1/video_data FIRST; for **layout edits** also call /v1/scene_geometry to pick coordinates from `boxes.remotion.object_layer.objects` (cheap, no screenshots). Use `voice_file` (stable per-scene UID, also base of `{voice_file}_spec.json`); `segment.id` is display/order only. **15 edit branches — pick ONE family per call (the only intentional multi-family call is `layout.batch`, which composes layout-only children)**: (A) Background media swap — `[{field_name:"mediaUrl", value:"<URL>"}, {field_name:"mediaType", value:"image"|"video"}?]`; roll-aware (B-roll updates mediaUrl/brollUrl, A-roll registers as brollUrl/user_asset_url). (B) Upload Overlay (FREE, agent-supplied asset → Remotion spec, NOT Regenerate which is paid) — `[{field_name:"remotion.upload_overlay", value:"<URL>"}]` or `value:{url}`. **Two upload formats, chosen by URL extension**: (1) **SVG path** — URL ends `.svg`, routes through `svg2spec`: viewBox `0 0 720 1280` required; each `<g data-wc-object="name">` group becomes one Storyboard object with **pixel-perfect placement (NO auto-fit; max diff 2/255 vs original)**; per-group attrs `data-wc-object` (REQUIRED stable id; unmarked groups become background), `data-wc-kind` ∈ {object,text,bar,mark,callout} (inferred), `data-wc-anim` ∈ {slide-up,slide-down,slide-left,slide-right,pop,grow-x,grow-y,fade,…} (default fade; bars get growRight/growUp), `data-wc-z` (paint order). Deterministic — no classifier in the loop. SVG errors → 422 `svg2spec_failed`; download → 502. PREFERRED for agent-authored overlays. (2) **Raster path** — PNG/JPG/WebP/GIF/etc; classifier-driven (graphic vs realistic) with strict no-AI fallback. Prefer 720×1280 transparent PNG or flat-bg graphic for best decomposition. Ground the asset in scene context (text/talking_point/visual/quote/keyword/type). (C) Remotion object-layer rect (FREE; **PREFERRED overlay layout**) — `[{field_name:"remotion.object.rect", value:{layout_id:"main.one_by_one"|"main.obj_03_text", x?, y?, w?, h?, coordinate_space:"preview"|"canvas"}}]`. Read `boxes.remotion.object_layer.objects` from /v1/scene_geometry first (each item has layout_id, rect 280×498, rect_canvas 720×1280, temporal_policy, update_field). For `one_by_one`, scene_geometry exposes ONE logical `*.one_by_one` rect that transforms all timed sequence items together; server keeps the group wrapper unchanged. (D) Remotion group rect (FREE; low-level wrapper edit; prefer (C) for visible overlay layout) — `[{field_name:"remotion.group.rect", value:{element_id?, x?, y?, w?, h?, coordinate_space:"canvas"|"preview", resize_mode?:"scale_children"|"wrapper_only"}}]`. Canvas = 720×1280 (NOT clamped — y:-120 OK); preview = 280×498 (converted). (E) Narrator layout rect (FREE) — `[{field_name:"overlay.narrator.rect", value:{x,y,w,h,visible?,animation?,borderRadius?}}]` or field-by-field via `overlay.narrator.x|y|w|h`. **280×498 preview coords**. Preserves narrator metadata + source-space `segment.narrator_face` (do NOT mutate narrator_face for layout — it's the source-space face box for narrator media; scene_geometry returns the displayed face converted through the current narrator rect). Marks `overlay.narrator.touched=true`. (F) Caption Y layout (FREE; vertical placement only) — `[{field_name:"overlay.caption.y", value:408}]`. 280×498. ONLY Y; no text/x/w/h/style/visibility/audio/duration/spec changes. (G) Layout batch (FREE; one persist + one MQTT scene_modified) — multiple layout fields directly OR `[{field_name:"layout.batch", value:{fields:[...]}}]`. Allowed children: overlay.narrator.*, overlay.caption.y, remotion.object.rect, remotion.group.rect. DISALLOWED in batch: mediaUrl/mediaType, voice.upload, narrator.upload_video, remotion.upload_overlay, roll.active/switch, segment.text, metadata. (H) Upload Voice (FREE; ASYNC) — `[{field_name:"voice.upload", value:"<audio URL>"}]`; returns `{object:"scene_voice_upload_queued", queue_id:"gs_{topic_id}_{voice_file}", status:"queued"}`. On completion server applies words/text/duration/timeline/captions/narrator_face/recorded flags and emits MQTT `event="scene_voice_upload_applied"`. (I) Upload Narrator Video (FREE; ASYNC) — `[{field_name:"narrator.upload_video", value:"<video URL>"}]`; returns `{object:"scene_narrator_upload_queued", ...}`. B-roll target → server preserves previous background as brollUrl/brollThumbnailUrl and applies the same roll-switch helper as `roll.active="A"` on completion. (J) A/B-roll switch (SYNC data switch) — `[{field_name:"roll.active", value:"A"|"B"}]` or `[{field_name:"roll.switch", value:"toggle"}]`. Preserves both lanes; swaps active runtime fields. A→B mirrors editor's `_switched` file-family protection. (K) Segment text correction — `[{field_name:"segment.text", value:"..."}]`. Rebuilds word timings over existing audio; does NOT change audio/duration/timeline. (L) Scene metadata — `pattern`/`visual`/`keyword`/`quote`/`talking_point`/`type`/`sub_mode` (`segment.<name>`/`scene.<name>` namespaced forms accepted). `pattern` validated against ai_segment_text canonical values; `type` ∈ {HOOK, STAT, KEY POINT, DATA, FACT, CALL TO ACTION}; `pattern="illustration"` requires `sub_mode` ∈ {photo_with_people, photo_no_people, document, digital_ui}; `pattern="narration_only"` auto-clears quote+visual; `pattern="typography_only"` auto-clears visual. (M) Remotion add element (FREE; SYNC; add-only) — `[{field_name:"remotion.add_element", value:{kind:"text"|"stat"|"label"|"callout"|"image", value?, label?, url?, position?:"top"|"bottom"|"left"|"right"|"center", rect?:{x,y,w,h,coordinate_space?}, style_token?, emphasis?, entry?, delay_sec?, z_index?, element_z_index?}}]` (or bare string for kind=text). Appends a new Storyboard group/object — does NOT auto-fit, replace, move, or modify existing objects. Must be sent ALONE (400 `mixed_remotion_fields` otherwise; not allowed inside `layout.batch`). Requires enabled spec (409 `remotion_spec_disabled` for `remotion_spec="none"`). Response `applied` returns new `element_id`/`object_id`/`layout_id` (= `{element_id}.{object_id}`)/`rect`/`rect_canvas`/`auto_fit:false`/`cost:"free_spec_append"`/`follow_up` hint, plus sets `remotion_element_added:true`. Standard workflow: call /v1/scene_geometry then issue `layout.batch` with `remotion.object.rect` for that layout_id to land the element inside safe zones. Errors: 400 `invalid_remotion_add_element`/`invalid_remotion_add_element_kind`/`mixed_remotion_fields`, 404 `remotion_spec_not_found`, 409 `remotion_spec_disabled`/`missing_voice_file`/`remotion_spec_parse_failed`/`remotion_spec_invalid`. (N) Disable overlay (FREE; SYNC; data edit) — `[{field_name:"disable_overlay", value:true}]` (aliases: `remotion.disable_overlay`/`overlay.disable`/`remotion_spec.none`; `value` may be `true`, the string `"none"`, or `{enabled:false}`). Sets `segment.remotion_spec="none"` (opt-out sentinel) and emits MQTT `scene_modified` with `overlay_disabled:true`. **Does NOT** delete `{voice_file}_spec.json` or `{voice_file}_overlay_poster.png`, does NOT regenerate, does NOT touch narrator/caption/media/timing/layout. Must be sent ALONE (400 `mixed_remotion_fields` if combined). Idempotent: re-disabling returns `applied.idempotent:true`. Re-enable via (B) Upload Overlay (writes fresh `{voice_file}_spec.json` and stamps `remotion_spec` to `{voice_file}_spec.json?v={mtime}`). Errors: 400 `invalid_disable_overlay_value`/`mixed_remotion_fields`, 409 `missing_voice_file`. `segment.remotion_spec="none"` = user intentionally disabled overlay (via (N) or UI); do NOT auto-enable; layout edits return `remotion_spec_disabled`. (O) Overlay TEXT edit (FREE; SYNC; 0-LLM; SVG-sourced overlays only) — `[{field_name:"overlay.text_edit", value:{wc_object:"<g data-wc-object id>", lines:["NEW LINE 1","NEW LINE 2"], fill?:"#1E6091"}}]` (`lines` may be a single string; `fill` is an optional hex colour repainting the group's main text; send lines and/or fill — a fill-only edit keeps the words; one or more fields, one per group). Rewrites `{voice_file}_overlay.svg` in place (face-stack copies update together; fewer lines delete slots, extra lines stack below), re-rasterizes ONLY the touched groups, patches the existing spec objects — layout/narrator-fit shifts/manual positions on other objects preserved. Requires `spec._source="svg2spec"` (endpoint posters / uploaded SVG overlays); typography and image scenes return 422 `no_svg_overlay_source` (typography: edit `quote` via (L) + regenerate). Poster copy rules (max 3 lines, max 4 words/line, uppercase) return as `applied.warnings` only. The `type="thumbnail"` clone of an edited opening poster is NOT auto-synced — apply the same edit to the thumbnail voice_file. Sent ALONE (400 `mixed_remotion_fields`). Errors: 400 `invalid_text_edit`/`missing_text_edit`, 404 `remotion_spec_not_found`, 409 `remotion_spec_disabled`/`missing_voice_file`, 422 `no_svg_overlay_source`. When `by="text"` matches multiple scenes → 200 `{object:"clarification", needs_input:"value", candidates:[{segment_id, voice_file, score, text}]}` — ask user, retry with `by="voice_file"`. Success (sync) → `{object:"scene_modified", id, scene_id, voice_file, score, applied, segment, layout_batch_updated?, narrator_layout_updated?, caption_layout_updated?, remotion_object_updated?, remotion_element_added?, overlay_disabled?, remotion_spec_updated?, remotion_spec_url?, remotion_spec_version?, remotion_spec_state?, remotion_poster_file?, remotion_poster_url?, remotion_poster_state?, media_type?, media_url?, uploaded_overlay_url?, roll_switched?, active_roll?, show_narrator?}`. Successful edits publish MQTT realtime to every open editor.
- POST `/v1/upload_asset` — **SYNC, no credit**. Get an audio / video / image / document (HTML / PDF / Markdown) asset into WideCast's S3 bucket and back out as a public URL (24-hour TTL — the `assets/` prefix has a lifecycle rule). Three shapes: **(1) multipart/form-data** with `file=@...` (SDK / curl / ChatGPT Action) → `{object:"asset", url, content_type, size_bytes, filename, expires_at, ttl_hours}`; **(2) application/json** with `{mode:"presign", filename, content_type?}` — **the canonical AI-agent / MCP path** (bytes never ride through the API) → `{object:"asset_presign", put_url, get_url, url, key, content_type, filename, headers_required, max_bytes, put_expires_at, expires_at, ttl_hours}`. The caller then does `curl -X PUT --upload-file <local_path> "<put_url>"` to push bytes straight to S3 (NO extra headers required — the signature only binds `host`, `headers_required` is empty by design so any HTTP client works as-is), then feeds `get_url` into create_video; **(3) application/json** with `{file_data:<base64>, filename, content_type?}` (legacy / small-file convenience) → same `AssetResponse`. Server cap **500 MB**; the MCP transport practically caps inline base64 to ~25 MB so MCP agents take the presign path. Allowed: `audio/*` + `video/*` + `image/*` + documents (`text/html`, `application/pdf`, `text/markdown`). **THIS is the canonical path** AI agents should use for files the user attached in chat → pass the returned `url` (or `get_url`) into /v1/create_video as audio_url / video_url, or inline as `![alt](url)` in script_text, OR `curl <get_url>` to read a document body before passing it as blog_text / script_text.
- POST `/v1/create_content` — written content: `{content, content_type, language}`. `content` = a URL/idea/text; `content_type` = `blog`|`facebook`|`x`|`linkedin` (default `blog`). Async → returns `result.review_url` (content viewer) in the create response itself, share immediately; poll `/v1/status` for completion. Charges credits.
- POST `/v1/create_image` — **SYNC, charges 1 credit per image** (count=4 → 4 credits). Generate 1-4 AI images from a text prompt: `{prompt (≤2000 chars, REQUIRED), ratio?: "portrait"|"landscape"|"square" (default portrait), count?: 1-4 (default 1), topic_id?}`. Same engine the dashboard's Gen-AI tab uses. **SCOPE — modify_scene workflow ONLY, NOT for new-video creation**: use to swap/replace ONE scene's media on an EXISTING video (the picked image → /v1/modify_scene `field_name="mediaUrl"`). For NEW scripts via /v1/create_video, do your own research and embed real URLs inline as `![](url)` per the writing-skill method — DO NOT pre-generate images here. → `{object:"image_set", status:"completed"|"partial", count, ratio, prompt, images:[{number, url, thumbnail_url, ratio}], request_id}`. **AGENT PRE-CALL: ALWAYS tell the user the cost FIRST** — surface a one-line notice in the user's language ("Heads up: this will use **1 credit** (each image = 1 credit)." for count=1; "Heads up: this will use **N credits** — N images at 1 credit each." for count>=2). For count>=2, require an explicit confirmation before calling ("Generate N variations for N credits — confirm?"). Never silently spend credits. **AGENT POST-CALL — show the image(s) so the user can actually SEE them**. ⚠ Most agent runtimes (Claude included) CANNOT render an external `https://…` URL inline in chat. Pick by **count**: **(A) count=1** → DOWNLOAD `images[0].url` locally + attach inline (Claude image-attach / Codex view_image after save). 1 fetch = safe. **(B) count>=2** → BUILD AN HTML ARTIFACT GALLERY with `<img src='URL'>` per image — DO NOT individually download / view each thumb (Pexels / Google / our S3 all rate-limit aggressively; N fetches in seconds → account may be banned). Splice URLs into the artifact, ask the user to pick by number, then `images[N-1].url` → widecast_modify_scene or inline `![](url)` in a future script. **(C) After user picks ONE** → 1 fetch is safe (download for high-res preview / confirm). The pattern is: N thumbs shown via artifact (0 fetches), pick 1, fetch 1. NEVER N results = N fetches.
- POST `/v1/search_broll` — **SYNC, FREE**. Search stock B-roll for a keyword: `{keyword (REQUIRED), kind: "video"|"image" (REQUIRED), ratio?: "portrait"|"landscape"|"square" (default portrait, only meaningful for kind=video), limit?: 1-20 (default 10)}`. Two modes — **kind="video"** (Pexels/Pixabay/Shutterstock CLIPS, broll.js Stock tab engine) and **kind="image"** (Google real PHOTOS, broll.js Photos tab engine). **Curated grid backgrounds (special branch — kind="video" only)**: when `keyword` is the EXACT single word `"grid"` (case-insensitive, no other words — phrases like `"grid background"` still hit normal stock search), the server SKIPS Pexels/Pixabay/Shutterstock and returns WideCast's curated internal grid-background video list in the SAME `results[]` shape. Shared `stock_video_from_text` engine handles both the UI Stock-tab grid keyword and this REST/MCP route. Use when the user asks for the WideCast template grid ('show me the grids', 'I want a grid background'). **SCOPE — modify_scene workflow ONLY, NOT for new-video creation**: use to find replacement media for ONE scene on an EXISTING video (the picked clip/photo → /v1/modify_scene `field_name="mediaUrl"`). For NEW scripts, do your own URL research inside the writing-skill 7-step method and embed inline `![](url)` — DO NOT call /v1/search_broll first to pre-pick visuals for a brand-new video (defeats the inline-URL discipline). Natural sequence: /v1/create_video → user reviews → user asks to swap scene N → /v1/search_broll → user picks → /v1/modify_scene. Prefer this over /v1/create_image when the user asks for a REAL-WORLD asset (landmarks, products, news events) — real footage beats AI generations for credibility. → `{object:"list", kind, keyword, ratio, total, results:[{number, type, url, thumbnail_url, title, source, duration, width, height, author?, context_url?}], request_id}`. **AGENT POST-CALL — MANDATORY rule**: BUILD AN HTML ARTIFACT GALLERY with `<img src='URL'>` per result. DO NOT individually download / view_image each thumbnail (Pexels / Pixabay / Google / Shutterstock all rate-limit aggressively; N requests in seconds → **account may be banned within a single search**). The artifact's `<img>` is loaded by the USER'S BROWSER once — no quota burn on the AI host or the source. Splice URLs only; for videos wrap `<img>` in `<a href='VIDEO_URL' target='_blank'>` so click → opens the clip. User picks by number; ONLY THEN may you fetch `results[N-1].url` (1 fetch = safe) to attach a preview or feed into widecast_modify_scene. NEVER N results = N fetches.
- POST `/v1/collect_ideas` — **SYNC**: `{product_service_input (≥10 chars), sub_industry?, user_location?, target_location?}`. `target_location` is the **audience market** (e.g. `"California, United States"`, `"Vietnam"`) — can differ from where the user lives. If omitted AND no cached one on the account, returns HTTP 200 `{object:"clarification", needs_input:"target_location", message}` (NO credit charged) — relay the message, then call again with the user's answer. On success → `{object:"ideas", ideas:[{title, description}]}`. Charges 1 credit only on success.
- POST `/v1/publish` — distribute to connected social platforms. Provide EXACTLY ONE of `topic_id` (an existing WideCast video/blog — a video must be rendered first), `text` (arbitrary post, +`photo_urls?`), or `video_url` (external direct video file url, needs `title`). `platforms?` defaults to ALL connected (`youtube|tiktok|instagram|facebook|linkedin|x|threads|pinterest|reddit|bluesky|google_business`). Charges 1 credit, posts PUBLICLY. → `{object:"publish", id, request_ids:[…], status:"processing", platforms, skipped}` (202). Poll `GET /v1/status/{request_id}` → `type:"publish"`, `result.posts:[{platform, success, post_url}]`.

### Read / library (all GET, SYNC, key-required, **0 credit**)
- GET `/v1/videos?from_record=0` — recent videos → `{object:"list", data:[{id,title,language,created_at}], total_count, from_record}`.
- POST `/v1/video_data` — **SYNC, FREE. First step for data-first scene audit/edit** — call before /v1/scene_geometry / /v1/modify_scene / /v1/scene_inspector. The recommended chain is **video_data → scene_geometry → modify_scene** (use scene_inspector only as an expensive last resort when you need browser truth / a small live screenshot). Body `{video_id (REQUIRED — topic_id; accepts widecast..., gubo..., or current ids), include_diagnostics?:boolean (default false)}`. **URL-RESPONSE CONTRACT (default `delivery_mode="download_url"`)**: HTTP response is a small envelope — the full video_data tree is published to a temporary public JSON file on `origin.widecast.ai` and the envelope carries `data.url`+`data.bytes`+`data.expires_at`+`data.ttl_seconds=900` (15-min TTL) plus a 3-step `instructions` block. **The agent must `mkdir -p ./.widecast-video-data && cd ./.widecast-video-data && curl -fsSL '<data.url>' -o video_data.json` then Read it locally** — the full tree is NOT inlined. Bypasses MCP per-tool-call output caps that previously truncated 50–300 KB payloads mid-JSON. Every call publishes a NEW unique file (16-hex token), so URLs are never reused (matches realtime semantics). Host is `origin.widecast.ai` (CF-bypassed) + `?v=<mtime>` cache-bust. Server only responds AFTER the JSON is fsynced + atomically renamed, so the URL is guaranteed readable. Operators can flip back to legacy inline mode via env flag `WIDECAST_VIDEO_DATA_DELIVERY_MODE=inline_content`. The published JSON file shape is unchanged from the legacy inline response: full annotated segment dicts with stable-identity + Remotion spec metadata. Trimmed to keep MCP payloads small: per-segment `words`, top-level `captions`, internal preview-cache fields are dropped. **Internal poster diagnostics stripped by default** — `remotion_poster_file`/`remotion_poster_url`/`remotion_poster_version`/`remotion_poster_state`/`remotion_poster_exists`/`remotion_poster_warnings` (and their copies inside `agent_meta.remotion_spec`) describe the server-side `{voice_file}_overlay_poster.png` used by scene_inspector — agents don't act on them. Pass `include_diagnostics:true` to surface for server/debug audits. **Scene identity rule** (also embedded as `scene_identity` in the published JSON): use `voice_file` as the stable per-scene UID; `segment.id` is display/order only. Spec file is `{voice_file}_spec.json`. **Per-segment fields**: `voice_file`/`scene_uid` (stable), `id`/`order_id`/`scene_index` (UNSTABLE), `type` (A-roll/B-roll/thumbnail), `text`/`talking_point`/`visual`/`quote`/`keyword`, `mediaUrl`/`mediaType`/`thumbnailUrl`/`videoTrim`, `overlay.caption`/`overlay.narrator` (legacy 280×498 editor coords), `remotion_spec` (`'none'` = user disabled overlay; do NOT auto-enable), `remotion_spec_file` (`{voice_file}_spec.json`), `remotion_spec_url` (cache-busted `?v=<mtime>`), `remotion_spec_version`, `remotion_spec_exists`, `remotion_spec_state` (`ready`/`missing`/`disabled`), `agent_meta` (bundled metadata). **Coordinate warning**: Remotion spec = 720×1280 canvas; legacy overlay rects = 280×498 preview. Spec content NOT inlined (large base64) — fetch `remotion_spec_url` only when state=`ready` and you need object boxes. Same engine the scene editor uses on open. Errors: 404 `video_not_found`, 409 `script_not_ready`, 500 `video_data_publish_failed` (disk write failed).
- POST `/v1/scene_geometry` — **SYNC, FREE, read-only**. Data-only layout geometry for ONE scene. Use AFTER /v1/video_data and BEFORE /v1/modify_scene or /v1/scene_inspector. Body `{id (topic_id, REQUIRED), voice_file? (preferred shortcut), scene_id? (fallback), by? + value? (only if shortcuts not used), min_score?, include_diagnostics?:boolean (default false)}`. Resolves the scene, loads `{voice_file}_spec.json` if available, and returns narrator / caption / Remotion Storyboard display boxes in one **280×498 editor-preview** coordinate space. Default response returns: `coordinate_space` `{width:280, height:498, unit:"editor_preview_px"}`; `safe_zones` (`dead_top` top 10%, `dead_bottom` bottom 25%, `safe_rect`); `scene` `{text, talking_point, type, pattern, keyword, visual, quote, show_narrator, active_roll}`; `boxes.narrator` `{rect, visible, face_source, face (displayed, converted through current narrator rect), face_center}` — **do NOT mutate `segment.narrator_face`** for layout edits; `boxes.caption` `{container_rect, text_rect_estimate, visible}` — read-only (only `overlay.caption.y` is mutable); `boxes.remotion.object_layer.objects[]` = **agent-facing layer**, each item `{layout_id (e.g. main.one_by_one, main.obj_03_text), rect (280×498), rect_canvas (720×1280), temporal_policy, update_field:"remotion.object.rect"}` — for `one_by_one`, ONE logical `*.one_by_one` rect transforms all timed sequence items; `boxes.remotion.groups[]` / `objects[]` / `sequence_objects[]` lower-level debug; `remotion_spec` metadata (internal `remotion_poster_*` keys stripped); `summary` `{remotion_object_count, remotion_object_layer_count, remotion_sequence_object_count, remotion_group_count, remotion_temporal_policies, remotion_geometry_basis}`. **Mechanical linter output is debug-only**. By default `violations[]` (collision codes), `warnings[]` (mobile-readability / face-staleness hints), `summary.error_count`, `summary.warning_count`, and `remotion_spec.remotion_poster_*` are stripped — vision-capable agents should judge collisions/aesthetics from a screenshot via /v1/scene_inspector; LLM-only agents proceed with the rects + `boxes.narrator.face` to keep overlays off the face. Pass `include_diagnostics:true` to opt in: violations include `remotion_object_overlaps_narrator_face` (error), `remotion_object_in_top/bottom_dead_zone` (warning), `remotion_group_in_top/bottom_dead_zone`, `caption_text_overlaps_narrator_face`; warnings include `remotion_object_too_small_for_mobile`, `narrator_face_outside_narrator`, `missing_narrator_face`. The mechanical collision math is approximate (rect-on-rect; no alpha/timing) — treat as hints, not ground truth. Designed for LLM-only agents: reason over JSON, then call /v1/modify_scene with `layout.batch` containing overlay.narrator.rect / overlay.caption.y / remotion.object.rect. Never broadcasts MQTT, never renders screenshots, never modifies the video. Multi-text-match → 200 ClarificationResponse. Errors: 404 `video_not_found`, 409 `script_not_ready`, 502 `script_parse_failed`, 500 `scene_geometry_failed`.
- POST `/v1/scene_inspector` — **SYNC, FREE**. Live browser inspector — **MORE EXPENSIVE than /v1/scene_geometry**; use only when data + geometry are not enough: typically when the agent needs browser truth (mounted DOM, computed boxes, current preview play state) or a small 280×498 visual screenshot / overlay-only audit. Do NOT use as the first step if /v1/scene_geometry already gives the boxes you need. Body `{id (topic_id, REQUIRED), action (REQUIRED), scene_id?, voice_file?, selector?, activate?, seek_seconds?, timeout_ms? (~7000ms default, capped 15000), probe_timeout_ms? (~800ms, capped 2000), options?}`. **Allowed actions**: `list_live_editors` | `list_instances` | `get_preview_state` | `get_scene_dom_snapshot` | `get_computed_boxes` | `screenshot_scene_280x498` | `overlay_poster` | `activate_scene` | `reload_preview` | `pause_preview` | `play_preview` | `seek_preview`. Server broadcasts MQTT probe to open editor tabs, elects ONE healthy foreground tab, sends command only to that tab. Presence ≠ usability (tabs on workflow page / different video / no mounted preview are ignored for scene-bound commands). **🖼 `screenshot_scene_280x498` response = temporary public URL (15-min TTL)**: full composite (background + Remotion overlay poster + narrator + caption). Regular JSON `SceneInspectorResponse` whose `result.screenshot` carries `{url: "https://origin.widecast.ai/downloads/<co>/<topic>/inspector/<voice>_<token>.jpg?v=<mtime>", mime_type: "image/jpeg", width: 280, height: 498, bytes: N, expires_at: "<ISO>", ttl_seconds: 900}`. Agent fetches the JPEG with a plain `curl <url>` (no Authorization header — the path is public, served by nginx). Each call publishes a **fresh** unique file (16-hex token); URLs are never reused across calls (realtime data semantics). Host is `origin.widecast.ai` (not `widecast.ai`) — bypasses Cloudflare so 15-min ephemeral URLs never get pinned in CF edge cache; `?v=<mtime>` is belt-and-suspenders. Server only responds AFTER the JPEG is `fsync`-ed + atomically renamed to its final path, so the URL is guaranteed readable when the response arrives. Storage: `/mnt/html/lcw/downloads/<co>/<topic>/inspector/<voice>_<token16>.jpg`. Server composites (no live editor → scene thumbnails + `{voice_file}_overlay_poster.png`) publish to the same URL contract — gut-check, not real render. Internal renderer diagnostics (`result.warnings[]`/`result.layers_used`/`result.used_assets`/`result.narrator_on_top`/`result.narrator_area_ratio` plus a top-level `fallback` block) have been removed 2026-06 — agents read the screenshot URL, not the compositor's working notes. **🎨 `overlay_poster` action (companion to screenshot)**: server composites ONLY the Remotion overlay poster on a solid black 280×498 canvas (no background image, no narrator, no caption). Purpose = let the agent audit the overlay's readability / typos / grammar / semantic / diacritic / glyph rendering / punctuation without the background photo acting as visual noise. Response shape mirrors screenshot but uses `result.overlay_poster.{url, mime_type, width, height, bytes, expires_at, ttl_seconds}` and adds `result.review_checklist` — an English reminder covering the 8 audit dimensions the agent should walk. Filename is STABLE (`<voice>_poster.jpg`, overwritten each call); `?v=<mtime>` bumps every write so the URL string is fresh in every response. Server still fsync+atomic-renames BEFORE responding. Errors specific to overlay_poster: 409 `overlay_not_available` (scene has no poster — `remotion_spec='none'` or spec not built), 500 `overlay_publish_failed`. Error envelopes: 404 `video_not_found`/`scene_not_found`, 409 `script_not_ready`/`overlay_not_available`, 502 `script_parse_failed`, 500 `screenshot_publish_failed`/`overlay_publish_failed`. **All other actions** return JSON `{object:"scene_inspector_result", status, code, result, ...}` as before. **No-editor path for non-screenshot / non-overlay-poster actions is graceful**: returns 200 `{status:"unavailable", code:"no_live_editor"|"no_active_editor"}` — fall back to /v1/video_data + /v1/scene_geometry + fetching `remotion_spec_url`. Non-screenshot success: `{status:"completed", code:"ok", selected_browser:{...}, result:{...action-specific}, editors?[]}`. **Prefer /v1/scene_geometry over `get_computed_boxes` for structural audits** — geometry is cheaper, always-available (no browser needed), and returns the same boxes plus collision violations and safe zones in pure JSON. No arbitrary JS eval. Prefer `voice_file` as the scene selector. Errors: 400 `unsupported_action` / `publisher_missing`, 404 `video_not_found`, 409 `overlay_not_available`, 500 `screenshot_publish_failed` / `overlay_publish_failed`.
- GET `/v1/account` — profile + credits → `{object:"account", plan, credits_remaining, valid_to, industry, connected_platforms, …}`.
- GET `/v1/analytics?period=last_week` — social analytics (SLOW) → `{object:"analytics", period, dashboard:{…}}`. period ∈ last_day|last_week|last_month|last_3months|last_year|custom.
- GET `/v1/roadmap?cycle=1` — content roadmap → `{object:"roadmap", cycle, total_completed, total_slots, weekly_quota, current_week, streak, weeks:[…]}`.
- GET `/v1/production_plan?page=0[&week_start=&week_end=]` — weekly plan → `{object:"production_plan", total, ideas:[…], topics:[…], …}`. (week range may backfill rows upstream.)
- GET `/v1/foundation_videos?industry=&sub_industry=&page=0` — curated foundation-video template library (proven starter angles for an industry; navigation/discovery aid, creates nothing). `industry` falls back to the account industry. → `{object:"list", data:[{id (template topic_id), title, description, thumbnail_url, industry, group}], total}`. Re-promoted 2026-07-13 (Round 30). Errors: 401 auth, 502 `read_failed`.
- (`/v1/recommendations` withdrawn from the public surface 2026-07-13, Round 30 — REST-only for the dashboard UI; use `/v1/collect_ideas` to brainstorm ideas.)

### Connections (connect / accounts / configure — key-required, **0 credit**)
- ~~POST `/v1/connect`~~ — withdrawn from MCP/SDK 2026-06-21 (Round 28). REST endpoint still serves the dashboard UI but agents should point users at https://widecast.ai/#setup to connect social platforms.
- GET `/v1/accounts` — connected platforms → `{object:"list", data:[{platform, username, status, connected_at}]}`.
- GET `/v1/platform_settings` — load publish settings → `{object:"platform_settings", settings:{platform:{…}}}`.
- POST `/v1/platform_settings` — `{platform, settings}` → save publish prefs (privacy/page/subreddit) → `{object:"platform_settings", settings}`.
- POST `/v1/mcp_token` — mint a **remote-MCP** connector URL → `{object:"mcp_token", token, url:".../mcp/<token>"}` (shown once; revocable with the key). Paste the `url` as a custom MCP connector in Claude Web / ChatGPT to drive WideCast by URL (no install). The connector endpoint `/mcp/<token>` speaks JSON-RPC (Streamable HTTP) and exposes the same tools as the local MCP.

### Notifications (push a self-notify message — key-required, **0 credit**)
- POST `/v1/notification/send` — **SYNC, no credit**. Push a self-notify notification to the user's OWN account. Self-notify only: recipient (email + Telegram chat) resolved server-side from the account, never accepted as input (no `to` / `chat_id` / `email` field). **Multi-channel**: EMAIL is the DEFAULT channel (always sent when the account has an email on file); if the user has ALSO completed `Connect Telegram` at https://widecast.ai/#setup, the SAME notification is ALSO sent to Telegram. `subject` (REQUIRED, ≤200 bytes) = email subject line + prepended in **bold** before the Telegram body. Edge cases: no email but Telegram connected → Telegram only (+ `note`); neither → 400 `no_delivery_channel`. Body: `{subject (REQUIRED), message (≤4000 bytes, plain text OR caption when photo/video is set — ≤1024 bytes as caption), parse_mode?:"Markdown"|"MarkdownV2"|"HTML" (formats body; subject always bold), photo_url?, video_url?}`. `photo_url` + `video_url` mutually exclusive. Rate-limited 60/hour/account. Response `{object:"notification", status:"sent"|"partial", subject, media_kind, delivery:[...] (channels delivered), email?:{status, recipient_email_masked}, telegram?:{status, chat_id_masked, telegram_message_id}, note?, setup_url?, request_id}` — `status="partial"` when some but not all attempted channels succeeded; a channel skipped for exceeding Telegram's byte limit carries `telegram.status="skipped"` (email still sent). Errors: 400 `missing_field`/`subject_too_long`/`no_delivery_channel`/…, 429 `rate_limited`, 502 `notification_send_failed` (all channels failed). (Renamed from `/v1/telegram/send` 2026-07-13 — email-default + subject added.)

## Request fields — `source` × `output_type`

`source` (enum, default `text`) — what input you provide, and the required companion field:

- `text` → `script_text` — a finished narration **80–500 words**, used VERBATIM (no AI rewrite). Over-max → rejected (`script_too_long`).
- `idea` → `idea_text` — a brief **5–1000 words**; the server writes the narration. Over-max → auto-truncated (`details.input_truncated_from`).
- `blog` → `blog_text` — an article **30–3000 words** to repurpose; same AI writer as `idea`. Over-max → auto-truncated.
- `video_url` → `video_url` — **any public http(s) URL**: a direct video-file link (S3 / R2 / transfer.sh / file.io / your CDN, etc.) OR a YouTube/TikTok/Facebook page URL, **≤ 5 min**. Loopback / private / link-local hosts rejected (`unsupported_media_url`).
- `audio_url` → `audio_url` — **any public http(s) URL**: same as above (direct audio-file link or a platform page URL), **≤ 5 min**. **This is the right path for "user attached a voice memo in chat":** ask the user (or upload-side automation) to drop the file on a public host — transfer.sh / file.io / S3 / etc. — and pass that URL.
- `video_file` / `audio_file` → multipart upload (**≤ 5 min, ≤ 100 MB**). Requires `multipart/form-data`, so these are SDK/playground-only — most chat agents can't attach a local file and should use the URL sources instead.
- **AI-agent path when the user attached a file in chat:** call `POST /v1/upload_asset` first (multipart) to push the file to WideCast's S3 bucket (`widecast-assets`, 24-hour TTL). The response carries a public S3 URL — pass it here as `audio_url` / `video_url`, or use it as an inline `![](url)` in `script_text`. Do NOT inline-base64.

`idea` and `blog` are **generative** sources (server writes the script). `text` is verbatim. Media sources (`video_url`/`video_file`/`audio_url`/`audio_file`) carry their own script.

**Inline media in `script_text` (source=text):** embed a direct image/video URL inside the script, right next to the sentence it should illustrate, in EITHER form: (a) **markdown image syntax** `![brief scene description](https://cdn.acme.com/photo.jpg)` — RECOMMENDED when you're driving an AI chat host (Claude / ChatGPT / Grok / Gemini), because the host renders the picture inline so the end-user can visually approve each scene before the script is submitted; the alt text doubles as the strongest scene anchor; or (b) a **raw URL** on its own line — `… https://cdn.acme.com/photo.jpg …` (backward compat). WideCast strips both forms from the spoken narration and uses the URL as that scene's visual instead of auto-sourced B-roll. Supported = direct file links ending in `.png/.jpg/.jpeg/.gif/.webp/.bmp/.avif/.svg` (image) or `.mp4/.webm/.mov/.m4v/.avi` (video), optionally with a `?query`. Page links (a YouTube/TikTok watch URL) are NOT inlined — use `source=video_url` to turn a whole clip into a video. Multiple URLs OK; scenes without one still get automatic B-roll. So when the user already has specific photos/footage, put their direct URLs into `script_text` rather than describing them.

`output_type` (enum, default `scene`) — how far down the pipeline to run:

- `text` — stop at the editable script (only valid for non-`text` sources; for media it = Remake / transcript extract). `result.review_url` opens the Script Editor.
- `scene` — stop at "scenes ready for review"; returns `result.review_url`. **This is the right default for almost everything.**
- `video` — run end-to-end to a final MP4; `result.video_url` set on completion (slow).

Optional fields: `language` (`English` | `Vietnamese`, generative only), `video_length` (`short` ≈90s | `normal` ≈3 min, generative only), `research_enabled` (bool, generative only), `callback_url` (HTTPS webhook — fires `video.processing` then `video.completed`/`video.failed`; signed `X-WideCast-Signature: t=,v1=` HMAC-SHA256 of `{t}.{rawbody}`; envelope `{event_id,event_type,created_at,api_version,data:<status>}`), `metadata` (object echoed back on status), `wait_for_render` (bool — block up to 60s before returning).

**Test webhooks with zero infra:** open `https://widecast.ai/webhook-test.html` → it gives a throwaway `callback_url` (`.../webhook_test/<inbox>`) and shows every delivery (payload + headers + signature-valid badge) live. Programmatic: POST to `/webhook_test/<inbox>` is captured; `GET /webhook_test/<inbox>` returns `{deliveries:[…]}` newest-first. Ephemeral (~1h, last 50). `/v1/publish` is sync (no webhook).

## Choosing `output_type` (guidance for agents)

Pick by `source` + intent — this avoids slow renders and gives the user a review step:

- `source=idea` / `blog` (or any content you generated) → use **`text`** (returns the AI-written script for the user to review/edit; that script IS what the narrator says).
- `source=video_url` / `audio_url` → use **`scene`**.
- `source=text` → use **`scene`** (`text` is invalid when the script is already supplied).
- Use **`video` ONLY when the user explicitly asks for the FINAL finished MP4.** "Make a video" on its own means `scene` (review-first), NOT `video` — rendering is slow and users usually export from the UI after reviewing.

## Status, polling & results

- `status` enum (LOCKED): `pending | processing | completed | failed`. (`pending` only covers the brief create→worker race; treat it like `processing`.) Branch on `status`, never on the free-form `stage`.
- `result.review_url` (e.g. `https://widecast.ai/#scene_editor?topic_id=widecast...`) — where the user reviews/edits scenes or the script. **Present as soon as the id is issued** (during `pending`/`processing` too, not just completion) — it's a stable id-keyed page, so surface THIS exact link to the user immediately; never link the bare homepage. **Append `&readonly=true`** for a public, sign-in-free, **iframe-embeddable** read-only player — embed that variant to show the result inline; the plain URL is the editor.
- `result.video_url` — the final MP4. Only set when `output_type:"video"` finished, or after `export_video`.
- A status poll should never 404 right after create — the server tracks issued ids for ~10 min and returns `pending` during the race.

## Errors

Envelope: `{ "error": { "type", "code", "message", "param?", "doc_url", "request_id", "details?" } }`. Surface `error.message` + `request_id` to users. Codes (v0.1.0, see OpenAPI for the live list):

- Auth (401): `missing_api_key`, `invalid_api_key`.
- Validation (400): `invalid_source`, `invalid_output_type`, `script_too_short`, `script_too_long`, `missing_idea_text`, `idea_too_short`, `missing_blog_text`, `blog_too_short`, `missing_video_url`, `missing_audio_url`, `missing_media_file`, `unsupported_media_url`, `media_too_long`, `file_too_large`, `invalid_language`, `invalid_video_length`, `invalid_research_enabled`, `telegram_not_connected`, `invalid_parse_mode`, `conflicting_media`, `invalid_photo_url`, `invalid_video_url`, `message_too_long`.
- Free-tier (402): `free_tier_limit_exceeded` — paid=0 accounts hit a 60-second narration cap (≈ 240 spoken words at 4 words/sec for text/idea/blog; 60 s media duration for audio_*/video_*). `error.details` carries `{free_tier_max_seconds, free_tier_max_words, words_per_second_estimate, pricing_url}`. Show the user the pricing_url + offer to shorten the input.
- Render/runtime: `account_expired`, `credit_exhausted`, `render_failed`, `unknown_error`, `scenes_not_ready`, `export_failed`, `telegram_send_failed`.

For HTTP 402 (`credit_exhausted` / `account_expired` / `free_tier_limit_exceeded`), `error.details` is populated with structured upgrade/wait info — for credit/expiry: `{upgrade_url, reset_at (or expired_at), current_plan, credits_remaining, credits_required, current_plan_quota, next_plan, next_plan_quota}`; for free-tier: `{free_tier_max_seconds, free_tier_max_words, words_per_second_estimate, pricing_url, spoken_word_count?, estimated_seconds?}`. AIs should present BOTH options to the user: wait until `reset_at` for the monthly quota to refresh, OR upgrade to `next_plan` (credit) / paid plan (free-tier) via `upgrade_url` / `pricing_url`.

## Full spec & try-it

- [OpenAPI 3.1 — JSON](https://widecast.ai/openapi.json) and [YAML](https://widecast.ai/openapi.yaml) — **canonical**; mirror at `https://widecast.ai/app/dashboard/openapi.json`.
- [Interactive playground](https://widecast.ai/playground.html) — submits + auto-polls + shows the review URL in one click.
- [Docs](https://widecast.ai/docs.html) and [Create-video reference](https://widecast.ai/endpoints/create-video.html).
- [Per-host setup guides](https://widecast.ai/claude.html) — [Claude](https://widecast.ai/claude.html) · [ChatGPT / Codex](https://widecast.ai/chatgpt.html) · [Gemini / Antigravity](https://widecast.ai/gemini.html) · [Grok](https://widecast.ai/grok.html) — wiring this API into an AI host (MCP / Custom GPT Action).

## SDKs & agent integrations

- **Python SDK** — `widecast` (thin, single-file; `video.wait()` handles polling). Repo: https://github.com/widecast
- **JS/TS SDK** — `@widecast/sdk` (Node 18+, Deno, Bun, browser).
- **MCP server** — `widecast/mcp-server/` in the repo. Self-contained (calls this REST API via `fetch`; only dep `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`). Run from source: `npm install` then `node /abs/path/widecast/mcp-server/dist/index.js`. Exposes `widecast_create_video`, `widecast_wait_for_video`, `widecast_get_status`, `widecast_export_video`, `widecast_modify_scene`. (NOT published to npm yet — do not `npx @widecast/mcp-server`.)
- **Authoring Skills** — `widecast/skills/` (video-script / blog / social-post writing). Teach a model to write a strong script; pair with the MCP server (or this API) to turn it into a video. Skills = write well; the API/MCP = operate WideCast. **For `video` format, master `SKILL.md` is a small INDEX; detail lives in submodules** (`method` / `formats` / `hooks` / `ctas` / `research_visuals` / `handoff`). Call `GET /v1/skills/writing?format=video&module=<id>` to lazy-load a submodule. The entry response carries `available_modules[]` (auto-discovered from disk per format) + an always-returned `contract` field (~1.5 KB) that survives runtime truncation. Drop new `.md` files under a format folder and they appear instantly. Blog and social formats are still single-file today; the same `module` param works when sub-modules are added. **Editing Skill — DOWNLOAD-ZIP MODE (experiment, 2026-06-30)**: `widecast/skills/video-editing/` is the AI-video-editor playbook for refining EXISTING videos (master `SKILL.md` ~14 KB INDEX + 5 core modules `01_critical_rules`/`02_jump_prevention`/`03_dod_gates`/`04_principles_workflow`/`05_quality_qa_priority` + per-scene modules + style libs). **`GET /v1/skills/editing` does NOT return content inline** — it returns (a) a `preload_tools` hint block + (b) a 4-step download instruction. **(a) Preload tools first**: response carries `preload_tools.one_shot_query` (literal `select:widecast_video_data,widecast_scene_geometry,...` string covering EVERY WideCast tool), `preload_tools.broad_query`=`widecast` + `broad_max_results`~30 fallback, and `preload_tools.tools[]` with per-tool `why` extracted from each tool's own MCP description. Some MCP hosts (Codex, Claude Code) default to NARROW ToolSearch queries and silently drop critical tools like `widecast_modify_scene` — agent MUST run ToolSearch with `one_shot_query` BEFORE editing, otherwise the flow fails mid-run. The list is auto-derived from `_WC_MCP_TOOLS` registry at request time → adding a new tool is zero-config. `preload_tools` ships in BOTH delivery modes. **(b) Then download**: (1) `mkdir -p ./.widecast-skill-video-editing && cd ./.widecast-skill-video-editing`, (2) `curl -fsSL <result.download.zip_url> -o video-editing.zip`, (3) `shasum -a 256` matches `result.download.sha256`, (4) `unzip -o video-editing.zip`. Agent then reads `./video-editing/SKILL.md` from local disk and follows its LOAD MAP. Local-file reading consistently beats tool-result reading for step adherence (background audit, screenshot show-local, gate verdicts). The zip is hosted at `origin.widecast.ai` (Cloudflare-bypassed) with `?v=<mtime>` cache-bust. Always-returned `contract` field (~1.5 KB) is the cross-cutting-rules safety net. **Host requirements**: local shell + curl + unzip + a file-reading tool. Cross-FS hosts (Read tool can't see bash sandbox FS) → use `cat`/`head` via bash. **Adding/editing modules**: drop `.md` under the folder + `bash deploy_widecast.sh` — no Flask restart for content-only changes (server mtime-caches the zip; new mtime → new sha256 → new URL). Restart only when `dashboard2.py` itself changes or env var flips. **Revert** to inline-content mode: env `WIDECAST_EDITING_DELIVERY_MODE=inline_content` + restart. Errors: 503 `skill_zip_unavailable` (zip missing on disk → re-run deploy).

## Conventions (locked — changing = breaking)

- snake_case JSON fields; ID format `widecast<alphanumeric>` (clients must NOT strip the `widecast` prefix; public id == internal `topic_id`).
- API key prefix `wc_live_*`. Every resource has an `"object"` marker.
- Headers on every response: `X-Request-Id`, `X-RateLimit-*`, `X-WideCast-Version`. Timestamps ISO-8601 UTC.
